description: Knowledge for browser automation, Playwright testing, localhost verification, screenshots, and web scraping safety.

sections.name: Web Automation with Playwright
sections.explanation_simple: Web automation controls a browser to verify flows that normal unit tests cannot see: navigation, forms, login screens, visual layout, screenshots, downloads, and localhost app behavior.
key_concepts: Playwright: browser automation framework for Chromium, Firefox, and WebKit
Locator: stable way to target elements by role, text, label, or selector
Headless mode: browser runs without a visible window
Screenshot verification: saves visual proof of rendered state
Network interception: inspects or mocks API calls
Localhost smoke test: checks a local app before delivery

code_examples.title: Playwright Localhost Smoke Test
code_examples.code:
from playwright.sync_api import sync_playwright

with sync_playwright() as p:
    browser = p.chromium.launch(headless=True)
    page = browser.new_page(viewport={'width': 1280, 'height': 720})
    page.goto('http://localhost:3000', wait_until='networkidle')
    page.screenshot(path='tom_logs/web_smoke.png', full_page=True)
    browser.close()

sections.learning_path: Install browser runtime -> open page -> locate elements -> assert behavior -> capture screenshots -> inspect network

sections.name: Safe Web Scraping and Downloads
sections.explanation_simple: Safe scraping respects authorization, robots rules where applicable, rate limits, file-size caps, and data privacy. For Tom, downloads and scraping should remain size-capped and approval-gated when they can touch the filesystem.
key_concepts: Robots and terms: site rules that may restrict scraping
Rate limiting: prevents excessive automated requests
File-size cap: prevents accidental large downloads
Structured extraction: parse tables/JSON instead of brittle string slicing
Approval gate: user confirmation before risky filesystem or network actions
sections.learning_path: Check authorization -> fetch safely -> parse structured data -> store bounded output -> verify result

topics.name: Web automation capability note
topics.content: Tom has web verification routes, but Playwright must be installed in the active Python 3.11 environment for full browser automation.
